before.stem: ww A79 year old patient, with a history of AF, presents to ED complaining of sudden onset severe abdominal pain. Imaging shows occlusion of the superior mesenteric artery. Which of the following structures is most likely affected:
options: Stomach 1% (x) First part of the duodenum 10%
before.explanation: The superior mesenteric artery supplies midgut structures including the duodenum (after the major duodenal papilla in the second part), the jejunum, the ileum, the caecum and appendix, the ascending colon and the proximal two-thirds of the transverse colon. Occlusion of the superior mesenteric artery restricts blood flow to these structures resulting in intestinal ischaemia. Vv

after.stem: A 79 year old patient, with a history of AF, presents to ED complaining of sudden onset severe abdominal pain. Imaging shows occlusion of the superior mesenteric artery. Which of the following structures is most likely affected:
warnings: Source page and external anatomy reference reviewed; remains an unapproved OCR draft.
after.explanation: The SMA supplies the midgut, including jejunum and ileum.
after.learningNote: The SMA supplies the midgut, including jejunum and ileum.
after.highYieldNote: The SMA supplies the midgut, including jejunum and ileum.

memoryAid.coreFact: The SMA supplies the midgut, including jejunum and ileum.

evidence.externalFinding: NCBI confirms jejunal and ileal supply by SMA.

before.stem: hd A patient presents following a fall. Imaging shows damage to the L1 nerve root. Which of the following muscles are most likely to be affected:
options: Transversus abdominis and rectus abdominis muscles 5%
Rectus abdominis and external oblique muscles 55%
Transversus abdominis and internal oblique muscles
before.explanation: The ilioinguinal nerve is formed from the anterior rami of L1. It innervates the internal oblique and transversus abdominis muscles and supplies skin over the upper medial thigh and the external genitalia. . Vv

before.stem: ww Regarding the uterine tubes, which of the following statements is CORRECT:
options: The uterine tubes open into the peritoneal cavity lateral to the ovaries.
Each uterine tube is approximately 5 cm long. 4%
The opening of the uterine tube is formed by the ampulla. 56%
The infundibulum is the narrowest part of the uterine tube. 9%
Ectopic pregnancies occur most commonly in the isthmus of the uterine tube. 8%
before.explanation: Uterine tubes project laterally from the superior uterus, extending to the lateral pelvic wall, passing superior to the ovaries and opening into the peritoneal cavity immediately lateral to the ovaries. Each tube is about 10 - 12 cm long and divided into four parts. The isthmus is the narrowest part. The infundibulum is the funnel-shaped opening which curves around the superolateral pole of the ovary which opens into the peritoneal cavity. Ectopic pregnancies most commonly occur in the ampulla, the elongated part of the uterine tube. 7 : : Vv

after.stem: Regarding the uterine tubes, which of the following statements is CORRECT:
options: The uterine tubes open into the peritoneal cavity lateral to the ovaries.
Each uterine tube is approximately 5 cm long.
The opening of the uterine tube is formed by the ampulla.
The infundibulum is the narrowest part of the uterine tube.
Ectopic pregnancies occur most commonly in the isthmus of the uterine tube.
warnings: Source page and external anatomy reference reviewed; remains an unapproved OCR draft.
after.explanation: Uterine tubes open into the peritoneal cavity lateral to the ovaries; the source gives 10–12 cm length, isthmus as narrowest, and ampulla as commonest ectopic site.
after.learningNote: Uterine tubes open into the peritoneal cavity lateral to the ovaries; the source gives 10–12 cm length, isthmus as narrowest, and ampulla as commonest ectopic site.

after.mnemonic: Tube opens laterally; ampulla is the common ectopic site.

memoryAid.coreFact: Uterine tubes open into the peritoneal cavity lateral to the ovaries; the source gives 10–12 cm length, isthmus as narrowest, and ampulla as commonest ectopic site.
memoryAid.mnemonic: Tube opens laterally; ampulla is the common ectopic site.

evidence.externalFinding: NCBI supports fallopian-tube anatomy; source-specific teaching retained.

before.stem: Ad A79 year old man presents to ED complaining of fever and left sided abdominal and back pain. Imaging reveals a large perinephric abscess. Which of the following most likely describes the fluid location:
options: Between the renal cortex and the renal capsule
Between the renal capsule and the perinephric fat 31%
Between the renal capsule and the renal fascia
Between the renal fascia and the paranephric fat 13%
before.explanation: Immediately external to the renal capsule is the perinephric fat completely surrounding the kidney. Surrounding the perinephric fat is the renal fascia, and external to the renal fascia is the paranephric fat. Aperinephric abscess is located in the perinephric fat between the renal capsule and the renal fascia. Vv

options: Between the renal cortex and the renal capsule

Between the renal capsule and the renal fascia
Between the renal fascia and the paranephric fat
warnings: Source page and external anatomy reference reviewed; remains an unapproved OCR draft.
after.explanation: Perinephric fat lies between the renal capsule and renal fascia; a perinephric abscess occupies this compartment.
after.learningNote: Perinephric fat lies between the renal capsule and renal fascia; a perinephric abscess occupies this compartment.

before.stem: we A patient is brought to ED following abdominal trauma. Your consultant performs a FAST scan in the department and identifies fluid in Morison's pouch. Where is Morison's pouch located:
before.explanation: The supracolic compartment lies above the transverse mesocolon and contains the stomach, liver and spleen. It lies largely under cover of the costal limits of the thoracic cage. The supracolic space can be arbitrarily divided into right and left supracolic spaces and subspaces. The posterior right subhepatic space (Morrison's pouch) separates the liver from the right kidney. Fluid (e.g. ascites or haemoperitoneum) accumulates here as it is the lowest dependant spaces of the peritoneal cavity from a wide range of causes. It is also a preferential site for metastases and abscesses. : 4 v

after.explanation: Morison's pouch is the posterior right subhepatic space between the liver and right kidney and is a dependent peritoneal recess.

memoryAid.coreFact: Morison's pouch is the posterior right subhepatic space between the liver and right kidney and is a dependent peritoneal recess.

evidence.externalFinding: NCBI supports the hepatorenal recess as a dependent peritoneal space; source explanation supplies exact relation.
